questions.question: A principal of Rs. 50000 is invested at simple interest for 8 years. If the per annum rate of interest is 12 percent, then what will be the amount after 8 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 50000

Time (T) = 8 years

Rate of Interest (R) = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P times R times T)/(100)

Amount (A) = Principal + Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (50000 times 12 times 8)/(100) 

⇒ SI = (480000)/(100)

⇒ SI = 48000

Amount (A) = Principal + Simple Interest

⇒ A = 50000 + 48000

⇒ A = 98000

**The amount after 8 years is Rs. 98000.**

questions.question: The compound interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 8% per annum compounded annually is Rs. 416. What is the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for the same period?

questions.question: A man lent out ₹14,000 at 5% and ₹19,000 at 6% simple interest per annum. His total income (in ₹) from the interest in 3 years is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest = (P₁ × effective rate 1) + (P₂ × effective rate 2)

Effective Rate = Rate × Time

Total Interest = (14000 × 15%) + (19000 × 18%)

Total Interest = 2100 + 3420 = 5520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal 1 (P₁) = ₹14,000, Rate 1 (R₁) = 5%, Time (T) = 3 years

Principal 2 (P₂) = ₹19,000, Rate 2 (R₂) = 6%, Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6b38849eb7537aaee3f625f076f630ce22661a3f277efb1397ac53e379d2dd3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (14000 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100 = 140 × 15 = ₹2100

⇒ SI₂ = (19000 × 6 × 3) ÷ 100 = 190 × 18 = ₹3420

⇒ Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ Total Interest = 2100 + 3420 = ₹5520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after T years is given by A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Effective Rate Method

For Simple Interest, the effective rate for T years is simply R × T%. Here, 5% for 3 years becomes a 15% flat interest rate on the principal.

questions.question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹824 for a period of 4 years at the rate of 8% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for 4 years at 8% per annum = 8% × 4 = 32%.

This means 32% of the principal amount equals ₹824.

⇒ 1% of Principal = 824 ÷ 32 = ₹25.75

⇒ 100% of Principal = 25.75 × 100 = ₹2575

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2575.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Where P is the Principal amount.

 
 Principal (P) = 100%

 
 SI = ₹824
 Rate = 8% × 4 = 32%
 
 

 32% of P = ₹824

**Calculations:**

⇒ 824 = (P × 8 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 824 = (P × 32) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (824 × 100) ÷ 32

⇒ P = 82400 ÷ 32

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after a certain period is the sum of the Principal (P) and Simple Interest (SI): A = P + SI = P × (1 + RT/100).

Effective Interest Rate

In simple interest, the effective rate for multiple years is directly proportional to time. For 't' years at 'r'% rate, the total interest is (r × t)% of the principal amount.

Difference Between SI and CI

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal sum, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.

questions.question: What is that rate of simple interest at which a sum of money becomes three times of itself in 24 years?

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Amount after 24 years = 3P

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount - Principal

SI = 3P - P

SI = 2P

SI = P × R × 24 / 100

⇒ 2P = P × R × 24 / 100

⇒ 2 = R × 24 / 100

⇒ 2 = 24R / 100

⇒ 2 × 100 = 24R

⇒ 200 = 24R

⇒ R = 200 / 24

⇒ R = 8.33%

**The rate of simple interest is 8.33%.**

questions.question: The simple interest received on a sum for 5 years is 2/5 of the sum. What is the annual rate of interest?

Cancel out Principal from both sides:

Cross-multiply to solve for Rate:

⇒ Rate × 25 = 200

⇒ Rate = 200 / 25

⇒ Rate = 8

**∴ The annual rate of interest is 8 percent.**

questions.question: A person borrows ₹ 75,000 for 3 years at 5% simple interest. He lends it to B at 7% for 3 years. What is his gain (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net interest rate gain per year = 7% − 5% = 2%

Total gain percentage over 3 years = 2% × 3 = 6%

Gain amount = 6% of Principal (₹75,000)

⇒ Gain = 75,000 × (6 ÷ 100) = ₹4,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹75,000

Time (T) = 3 years

Rate of borrowing (R₁) = 5% per annum

Rate of lending (R₂) = 7% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Gain = SI Received − SI Paid

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0c3707c4f8189066c5e86346830e97cc05ea02e7502f431b4b1222a7e19a131.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest paid = (75,000 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest paid = 750 × 15 = ₹11,250

⇒ Interest received = (75,000 × 7 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest received = 750 × 21 = ₹15,750

⇒ Total gain = 15,750 − 11,250 = ₹4,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Interest is calculated only on the principal amount throughout the tenure. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest is calculated on the principal plus any previously accumulated interest. Amount = P × (1 + R/100)T.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, Difference = P × (R/100)². For 3 years, Difference = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

questions.question: The simple interest received on a certain sum is Rs.1782 for 3 years. What will be the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate of interest for 10 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simple interest (SI) for 3 years = Rs. 1782

**Concept:**

Simple interest is directly proportional to time when the principal and rate of interest are constant.

**Formula Used:**

SI = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

Since principal and rate are constant, SI ∝ Time

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ SI for 3 years = Rs. 1782

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1782 / 3

⇒ SI for 1 year = Rs. 594

Now, we need to find the SI for 10 years:

⇒ SI for 10 years = 594 × 10

⇒ SI for 10 years = Rs. 5940

**∴ The simple interest on the same sum at the same rate of interest for 10 years is Rs. 5940.**
